The table shows the amount of direct taxes that different households in the UK paid in 2017–2018. bottom second middle fourth top 20% of 20% of 20% of 20% of 20% of households households households households households average 15300 25000 34600 47600 90600 income (£) direct tax 2000 3500 6000 9500 21200 paid (£) Which positive economic statement can be made from the table?

options.A: Direct tax is unfair on the richer households in the UK.
options.B: Direct tax in the UK is a proportional tax.
options.C: Poorer households do not pay enough direct tax in the UK.
options.D: Rich households pay more direct tax than poor households in the UK.

questions.questionText: What does opportunity cost measure?

options.A: the benefits of a good compared with the next choice
options.B: the benefits given up by not consuming the next best alternative
options.C: the costs of any good not chosen
options.D: the financial costs of consuming a good

questions.questionText: Which term assumes the existence of ‘qualities, knowledge and skills’ that allow an individual to be more productive?

options.A: enterprise investment
options.B: human capital
options.C: mechanisation
options.D: specialisation

questions.questionText: The diagrams relate to the markets for four different products. In which market would a 10% decrease in demand and simultaneously a 10% increase in supply definitely result in both a fall in equilibrium price and a rise in equilibrium quantity?

options.A: B S S price price D D O O quantity quantity
options.C: D D S price price S D O O quantity quantity

questions.questionText: The supply of a new drug to relieve muscle pain is very inelastic over a short period of time. The supply of printed newspapers is much more elastic over the same time period. What could explain the difference in elasticity of supply of the drug and printed newspapers in this time period? new drug printed newspapers

options.A: cost per unit is low cost per unit is high
options.B: discovery is by chance takes longer to produce
options.C: research and development essential excess capacity in printing
options.D: similar products available similar products unavailable

questions.questionText: Which change would cause the supply curve of sugar-sweetened drinks to shift to the right?

options.A: a fall in the price of sugar
options.B: a removal of a subsidy on sugar
options.C: an increase in consumer income
options.D: an increase of a specific tax on sugar

questions.questionText: The demand for tablets increases, while the cost of producing them decreases. What will be the effect on the price of tablets and on the quantity supplied? price quantity

options.A: fall uncertain
options.B: rise increase
options.C: uncertain increase
options.D: uncertain uncertain

questions.questionText: What is necessary to achieve the best allocation of resources using the price mechanism?

options.A: Producers can maximise their collective interest.
options.B: Consumers and producers must have perfect knowledge.
options.C: The government must be able to apply maximum and minimum prices.
options.D: The value of the price elasticity of supply must be greater than one.

questions.questionText: Goods X, Y and Z all have downward-sloping demand curves and upward-sloping supply curves. Good X is in joint supply with good Y and in joint demand with good Z. There is an increase in the demand for good X. What will happen to the prices and sales of goods Y and Z? good Y good Z price sales price sales

options.A: fall fall rise rise
options.B: fall rise rise rise
options.C: rise fall fall rise
options.D: rise rise fall fall

questions.questionText: What is meant by consumer surplus?

options.A: It is the amount by which the price consumers are willing to pay exceeds the market price.
options.B: It is the difference between the price consumers are willing to pay and the price producers are willing to supply.
options.C: It is the discount firms offer to the consumers for buying goods in bulk.
options.D: It is the excess of quantity demanded of a product over its quantity supplied at a given price.

questions.questionText: What does the assumption ‘ceteris paribus’ mean when economists analyse the way in which the quantity demanded of a good changes?

options.A: Changes in quantity demanded can cause changes in any of the other variables.
options.B: Consumer preferences are always assumed to remain unchanged.
options.C: Only one variable is assumed to change while the others remain the same.
options.D: Several variables change simultaneously.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand curve for a normal product. price W X demand Y Z O quantity Which two points indicate a move from a price inelastic point to a less price inelastic point?

options.A: W to X B X to W C Y to Z D Z to Y

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the effect on the market for rice of a change in government policy that causes a shift in the supply curve from S to S .

The table shows four categories of government expenditure over two time periods. period 1 period 2 category ($000) ($000) building of new roads 200 350 welfare benefits 600 450 pay of armed forces 500 550 state pensions 1100 1350 By how much had transfer payments changed between periods 1 and 2?
Which type of tax used in different countries is a direct tax?

options.A: corporation tax in India that is imposed on the profits of companies
options.B: import duties in Brazil that are imposed on imported goods
options.C: specific tax in South Africa imposed on the purchase of cigarettes
options.D: stamp duty in Malaysia that is the tax on the purchase of a residential property

questions.questionText: A government imposes a maximum price on medical face masks, below the market equilibrium. What is the most likely effect of this?

options.A: Some consumers will be unable to buy face masks at the maximum price.
options.B: Firms will produce more masks to meet the excess demand at the maximum price.
options.C: Poorer consumers will be able to obtain all the masks they need at the maximum price.
options.D: The market will clear at the maximum price.

questions.questionText: What is not a producer subsidy?

options.A: a grant given to cover losses in an essential industry, such as the rail industry
options.B: a guaranteed minimum price paid to farmers to ensure the long run supply of food
options.C: financial assistance given to a pharmaceutical company to develop a new vaccine
options.D: a payment made to the unemployed to allow them to buy essential goods and services

questions.questionText: The diagram shows an aggregate demand (AD) curve. Y AD O X What is measured on the horizontal (X) axis and the vertical (Y) axis? horizontal axis X vertical axis Y

options.A: money national output real disposable income
options.B: price level real GDP
options.C: real GDP price level
options.D: real disposable income money national output

questions.questionText: What could explain an improvement in the terms of trade for a country?

options.A: an increase in tariffs on imports
options.B: a decrease in the volume of imports sold
options.C: an increase in the prices of exports
options.D: a decrease in the volume of exports sold

questions.questionText: What is a correct description of an aggregate demand (AD) curve?

options.A: It is a curve obtained by adding the market demand curves of all consumer goods traded in an economy.
options.B: It is a curve determined by the horizontal summation of all individual consumer demand curves for a product.
options.C: It is a curve that shows the total amount of goods and services firms are willing to buy at a given price in an economy.
options.D: It is a curve that shows the total demand of all goods and services produced at all price levels in an economy.

questions.questionText: The data in the table is extracted from the Singapore Balance of Payments for 2019. $m goods balance +134000 services balance +8000 capital and financial account (net) +95000 balancing item –3000 What was the value ($m) of the trade balance on the current account in 2019?
A household’s income increased by 3%. Over the same period, the rate of inflation was also 3%. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Both the nominal income of the household and the real income of the household increased by 3%.
options.B: The nominal income of the household remained unchanged while the real income of the household increased by 3%.
options.C: The nominal income of the household increased by 3% while the real income of the household remained unchanged.
options.D: The nominal income of the household increased by 3% while the real income of the household increased by 6%.

questions.questionText: A country operates a fixed exchange rate. There is a major fall of international confidence in its government’s economic policies. What is likely to be the result?

options.A: a fall in its foreign exchange rate
options.B: a fall in its foreign exchange reserves
options.C: a rise in its capital inflows
options.D: a rise in its terms of trade

questions.questionText: In 2018, the inflation rate in Argentina was over 100%. Which combination correctly identifies the winners and losers during this period? winners losers

options.A: firms selling goods households paying back abroad loans
options.B: firms unable to decrease firms paying back loans on real wages fixed monthly repayments
options.C: individuals with a high amount households that hold most of debt at a fixed rate of interest of their assets in cash
options.D: workers on fixed the retired on fixed wage contracts incomes

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the aggregate demand (AD) and aggregate supply (AS) for a country. The initial equilibrium is at point E. The sum of the price elasticities of demand for imports and exports for this country exceeds one.

options.A: B E
options.D: C AD O real output

questions.questionText: In 2000, Japan was Asia’s largest exporter of electrical components, but by 2018 it was ranked 8th. What might explain this change?

options.A: Japan has a lower opportunity cost in electrical component production than its Asian competitors.
options.B: Japan has experienced greater deflation than its Asian competitors.
options.C: Japan has imposed tariffs on the import of electrical components from its Asian competitors.
options.D: The Japanese Yen has appreciated against the currencies of its Asian competitors.

questions.questionText: Which measure to correct a balance of payments current account deficit would be classified as an expenditure-reducing policy?

options.A: a reduction in interest rates
options.B: a revaluation of the currency
options.C: an increase in direct taxes
options.D: an introduction of foreign exchange controls

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the AD/AS curves for an economy. AS price level AS X Y AD AD O real GDP Which government action is most likely to cause the equilibrium position to move from X to Y?

options.A: an increase in the exchange rate that makes locally produced goods less price-competitive, both at home and abroad
options.B: an increase in government spending on infrastructure that increases the production potential of the economy
options.C: an increase in interest rates that increases the cost of borrowing
options.D: an increase in real wages of labour

questions.questionText: A country is suffering from severe deflation. What is most likely to prevent the deflation from worsening?

options.A: increasing income tax to help reduce the government’s budget deficit
options.B: increasing interest rates to encourage more saving
options.C: increasing transfer payments to reduce inequality of income
